dispositions.reason: The plan's Risks section already states the departure and why: AC-TESTS.md may map only new files, so two new test files in the same unit and integration suites keep the intent and leave existing tests untouched; no plan change is needed.

The refusal names each cause the reader actually observed; an invalid line after the cap is never read, so only the cap is named, which is still a correct and actionable message, and the build does not need a change.

Stopping at the abort check is how collect already behaves with --duration-ms or SIGINT; quality covers what was read, which the plan keeps unchanged, so this is an accepted bound and at most a wording nicety for tools.md.

This concerns how the test stage writes AC-5 (pin absolute expected counts from the clean recording rather than compare with old code), not the plan; the plan's acceptance mapping names the unchanged inputs and the test stage owns the baseline values.
